findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password check whenever totpCode is non-empty
findings.body: The password is only verified when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch (line 131) runs whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty, regardless of totpCode. A request that sends email, a valid 10-character backup code, and any non-empty totpCode is authenticated without the password, and the TOTP is never checked either. The login UI clears totpCode in lost-access mode, but the NextAuth credentials endpoint can be called directly. The TOTP branch already has the same password-skip pattern, but this PR adds a second path that needs only the backup code. Password verification should run for CAL users in every branch, so that the backup code or TOTP is an additional factor rather than a replacement for the password.

findings.title: Backup codes can be dismissed without being saved; 2FA is left enabled with the UI out of sync
findings.body: The codes are shown only in the DisplayBackupCodes step, which is reached after the enable endpoint has already set twoFactorEnabled=true. The Dialog still receives `onOpenChange`, so Escape, an overlay click, or the X button closes the modal without calling `onEnable` or the 'Close' button. The codes are never rendered again and there is no endpoint to retrieve or regenerate them, so they are lost. The parent is not notified that 2FA is on, so its switch stays unchecked. Toggling it again then fails in setup with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. If the authenticator is later lost, the user has no recovery path. The step should ignore dismissal (or require an explicit acknowledgement), and the dismissal path should still notify the parent.

findings.title: Backup code single-use is not enforced atomically
findings.body: Consumption is a read-decrypt-null-encrypt-write sequence with no transaction or compare-and-set on backupCodes. Two concurrent logins with the same valid code can both read the unconsumed array (line 139), both pass the indexOf check, and both write back, so one backup code yields two sessions. The whole-array write can also resurrect codes that a concurrent disable (which sets backupCodes to null) just cleared. Use a conditional update (for example, compare the old encrypted value in the WHERE clause and check the updated row count) or a transaction with row locking.

findings.title: Users who arrive via external-provider TOTP cannot use backup codes
findings.body: When totpEmail is set (2FA for a Google/SAML sign-in), the footer is only ExternalTotpFooter (Cancel), so there is no 'Lost access' action. The server also blocks backup-only submissions for non-CAL users: in authorize, the ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled check (next-auth-options.ts line 113) fires whenever totpCode is empty. A CAL user who has backup codes and then signs in with Google using the same email goes through loginWithTotp, so they can never use their backup codes and have no recovery path besides their authenticator. Either expose backup codes in this flow and allow a backupCode to satisfy the non-CAL check, or document the limitation.

findings.title: tabIndex=-1 removes keyboard access to the password visibility toggle in every PasswordField
findings.body: This change is unrelated to backup codes but applies to the shared PasswordField component used across the app. Setting tabIndex to -1 makes the show/hide button unreachable by Tab, so keyboard-only users cannot reveal a password they are typing. This is an accessibility regression. Drop the change or justify it separately.

findings.title: No tests exercise backup-code login, backup-code disable, or single-use consumption
findings.body: The new server logic (backup-code branch in authorize, backup-code branch in disable.ts, code consumption, MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode errors) has no test coverage. The PR checklist says no tests were added, and the only addition is a TODO. The enable/disable e2e flow only checks the download, copy, and close buttons. A regression in backup-code verification or single-use enforcement would go unnoticed, and the password-bypass issue above would not be caught. Add tests for: login with a valid code (consumed afterwards), reuse of a consumed code, wrong code, and disable with a backup code.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle does nothing because the caller's type="password" overrides PasswordField's type
findings.body: PasswordField renders `<InputField type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"} ... {...props} />`, so props spread after the computed type. Passing `type="password"` here (replacing the former TextField) forces the input to stay masked. The eye button toggles its icon and label, but the field never shows the password. Remove the explicit type prop.

findings.title: Assertion is vacuous: expect(promise).toBeTruthy() always passes
findings.body: `isChecked()` returns a Promise, so `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` checks that a Promise object is truthy and always succeeds. The FIXME above it acknowledges this. The PR edits this block but keeps the vacuous check, so the enable test does not verify the switch state. Use `await expect(page.locator(...)).toBeChecked()`.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes text tells locked-out users to generate codes in settings, which is not possible
findings.body: The message 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' is shown on the login page, where the user is not authenticated. There is no 'generate' action in settings: codes are created only by disabling and re-enabling 2FA, which itself needs a password and TOTP or a backup code. The message points users to a non-existent action.

findings.title: Copy button reports success without awaiting the clipboard write
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` is neither awaited nor caught, and the success toast is shown immediately. If the write is rejected (permissions, insecure context), the user still sees 'Backup codes copied!' and the rejection is an unhandled promise rejection. Await the write inside try/catch and show an error toast on failure.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code in lost-access mode fails silently
findings.body: With an empty backupCode and empty totpCode, authorize() skips the backup branch and throws SecondFactorRequired. The client handler then calls setTwoFactorRequired(true), which is already true, so nothing changes and no error is shown. The HTML required attribute is disabled by noValidate, and the zod schema does not cover backupCode. Validate that backupCode is non-empty before submitting, or show an error when this case occurs.
